facts.raw_span: A 34-year-old White woman with a history of obesity presented after an unwitnessed cardiac arrest
She was found unresponsive, and bystander cardiopulmonary resuscitation was initiated
She had mechanical intubation for airway protection and developed atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response
frequent premature ventricular contractions triggering polymorphic ventricular tachycardia and resultant hemodynamic collapse
No other specific physical examination findings were documented in the case report
Laboratory data showed no electrolyte derangements
Troponin T: 0.847 µg/L (normal, ≤0.01 µg/L)
Troponin I: 0.13 ng/mL (normal, ≤0.04)
Urine toxicology, alcohol, and acetaminophen screening results were negative
ECG showed sinus tachycardia with heart rate 101 beats/min, QTc 443 ms
Transthoracic echocardiogram: normal biventricular size and function, no significant valvular dysfunction, no pericardial effusion, no intracardiac shunt after agitated saline injection
Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging: mild left ventricular and left atrial dilation, preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (62%), no edema or late gadolinium enhancement
